title: Maximum Bitwise AND After Increment Operations
summary: Given an integer array nums, integers k and m, you can increment any element at most k times.
statement: Given an integer array nums, integers k and m, you can increment any element at most k times. Determine the highest possible bitwise AND of any m elements after optimally performing these operations.
constraints: nums has up to 50,000 positive integers; choose exactly m positions.
At most k total operations may increment chosen or unchosen elements by one.
Maximize the bitwise AND of the m chosen final values.
known_wrong_solutions:
def maximum_and_after_increments(nums,k,m):
    values=sorted(nums,reverse=True)[:m]
    answer=values[0]
    for value in values[1:]:answer&=value
    return answer+k
def maximum_and_after_increments(nums,k,m):
    answer=0;limit=(max(nums)+k).bit_length()
    for bit in range(limit-1,-1,-1):
        target=answer|(1<<bit);costs=[]
        for value in nums:
            missing=(target&~value).bit_length();mask=(1<<missing)-1
            costs.append((target&mask)-(value&mask))
        costs.sort()
        if max(costs[:m])<=k:answer=target
    return answer
hints: Build the answer from high bits to low bits, keeping a bit only when some m values can be raised to contain all chosen bits.
For a target mask and value x, only bits through the highest target bit missing from x need change before the next feasible number is reached.
Compute that increment cost per value, select the m smallest, and compare their sum with k.
High-to-low greedy is valid because feasibility is monotone under removing target bits, and accepted higher bits dominate every combination of lower bits.
editorial: High-to-low greedy is valid because feasibility is monotone under removing target bits, and accepted higher bits dominate every combination of lower bits.

tests.explanation: Raising three and two to six costs seven and yields AND six.
Raising one and two to four lets three chosen values share bit four.
